lines.46: **3c · Creep vs SF 2.5 — a newly quantified named problem [Likely].** At SF 2.5 the HMPE bulk sections carry a **steady centrifugal load of 28–40% of rated break strength** (40% raw; 28% if the 30% strength derate is applied in sizing). Public guidance: keep sustained HMPE load **≤ ~20%** for multi-year life (SK78 ≈ 8 yr at 20% and 20 °C). The centrifugal load is genuinely sustained in the rotating frame — this is exactly the bad regime. Reaching 20% load needs SF ≈ 5, which cuts Vc by √2 and blows the reference mass ratio from **~41× to order ~800×** (Moravec form) — not a design, a refutation. So the honest outcomes are: (a) HMPE sections have a **creep-governed replacement cadence** costed into ops; (b) the **hybrid boundary shifts toward PBO** (aramid-class creep, 3–5× lower) for the high-stress fraction; or (c) some mix. This goes on the risk register with numbers, feeds the TP-001 creep series, and motivates **ST-002** (below). Per Rule 6, this joins the named hard parts.
